messages:
maya: Heads-up — we've updated the SLO burn-rate policy and are scheduling a short maintenance + controlled load test. Read below and ack if you see any conflicts.

maya: Quick summary of the policy change:
• New burn-rate threshold: 3x baseline sustained over 10m triggers a canary pause + incident open.
• Previous behavior was a soft page at 5x for 15m; this tightens detection to accelerate mitigation.
• Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/slo-burnrate

maya: Planned maintenance + load test:
• When: Tue Mar 30 2026 02:00 - 03:30 UTC (please convert to your TZ).
• Scope: Controlled query load against canary fleets in us-west-2 + eu-central-1; simulate routing failover for one availability zone; exercise KV-cache warmup paths.
• Expected impact: No planned customer-facing downtime. Canary traffic may see increased latency and elevated error-rate transiently. We'll pause promotions during the window.

alex: Quick Q — does the new detection trigger an automatic rollback or only pause and page SRE?

maya: It will pause canaries and open the incident. No automatic global rollback. Teams keep manual rollback/promote controls. :white_check_mark:

jonathan: Monitoring plan: I'll surface the following on a single glance dashboard — 99p latency, p50/p95, error-rate, kv-cache miss-rate, model-serve queue length, and token-serve time. Alert threshold: error-rate > 25% for 5m triggers paging.

priya: I'll draft customer-facing notices for top enterprise accounts and any active trials. Also tagging affected releases: please avoid scheduling new canary promotions between 01:30-04:00 UTC on Mar 30.

oncall-bot: Calendar event created: "SLO burn-rate policy rollout + loadtest" Tue Mar 30 02:00-03:30 UTC — invites sent to #eng-sre, #eng-runtime, #product-ops.

maya: Runbook abort snippets (putting here for quick access):
```
# abort loadtest
kubectl scale deploy/loadtest -n stress --replicas=0
# pause traffic to canary pool
infractl routing set-weight --pool canary --weight 0
# resume canaries
infractl canary resume --namespace staging
```

tanya: Acked — I'll be on rotation that night and can jump on the incident channel if anything spikes.

alex: Ack — disabling auto-promote for the window and will coordinate with release owners.

jonathan: I'll post dashboard links in this thread ~1h before start.

maya: Thanks. Anything else we should add to pre-checks? If not, react with :eyes: once you've read.

alex: :eyes:

priya: :eyes:

jonathan: :eyes:

oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-slo-burnrate-1798765432"
